design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 03 variant A « Outline / plan du livre » (the BINDING target: an indented tree list, each row = a mono kind tag + node title, depth shown by left indent + a hairline guide rail, relink rows marked ↪ « (reliaison) », the isolated Mort row at the bottom). Tags reuse the NodeBadge mark language; tokens from styles.css. Low-fi, light theme.

plan.goal: Offer an indented outline of the whole book as an alternative to the canvas — fast navigation and structural overview for long books — sharing selection and data with tree-canvas.

design_contract._binding: Rebuild § 03 variant A with design-system components; DS tokens win over prose.
design_contract.rows: Each row: a compact `NodeBadge` (or its mark + 3-letter mono tag SOM/CHX/PNJ/DÉC/PIÈ/MON/FIN/MORT) + the node title (--fs-row). Indentation by depth with a 1px var(--line-3) guide rail and var(--space-6) left step per level.
design_contract.relink_rows: A row reached by a relink/fuite edge renders with a ↪ glyph + a muted « (reliaison) » mono note, NOT as a duplicated subtree — it points back to the canonical node.
design_contract.special_rows: FIN rows use the double-border mark; the obligatory « Mort du personnage » row sits at the bottom with the gray-hatch mark and a muted « — isolée » note.
design_contract.interaction: Hover lightens the row and reveals a peek affordance; click selects (emits node:selected) and the row shows the accent selected treatment, mirroring canvas selection.
design_contract.empty_state: An empty/near-empty book still lists Sommaire + Mort and shows an inviting « + Première feuille » row (project-wide empty-state rule).

acceptance_criteria: The outline lists every node exactly once, ordered by traversal from the Sommaire, with depth shown by indentation + guide rail, read live from BookService.
Each row shows the node's kind (via mark/tag) and title; FIN rows use the double-border mark and the Mort row is shown isolated at the bottom.
A node reached via a relink/fuite edge appears as a single ↪ « (reliaison) » reference row — never as a duplicated branch — so cycles and convergences don't infinitely expand.
Clicking a row selects that node and emits node:selected{nodeId}; selection is shared with tree-canvas (selecting here highlights there and vice versa), with a single selected node at a time.
Switching between canvas and outline preserves the current selection and the open book; the view mode persists per book via UIPreferencesService and is not cloud-synced.
Renaming/adding/deleting nodes or edges elsewhere updates the outline live (node:* / edge:* events) without reload.
An empty or single-leaf book renders Sommaire + Mort plus an inviting affordance to add the first leaf (empty-state rule).
Rows render from design-system tokens, light theme; titles ≥ --fs-row; the outline is keyboard-navigable (up/down to move, Enter to select).
plan.walking_skeleton: Traverse the book from BookService starting at the Sommaire, render an indented list of rows with kind tag + title, dedupe relink targets into ↪ reference rows, click a row → emit node:selected. Subscribe to node:*/edge:* to rebuild. Reuse the canvas's selection source. No keyboard nav or peek polish yet.

iterations.goal: Faithful render of § 03 variant A: traversal-ordered indented rows with marks/tags, guide rail, relink reference rows, FIN + isolated Mort treatment; live binding to BookService + node:*/edge:* events; click-to-select shared with canvas.
Navigation polish: keyboard up/down/Enter, hover peek, collapse/expand subtrees, smooth canvas↔outline switch preserving selection + scroll; persist view mode via UIPreferencesService.

known_risks: KR-030 — Relink/cycle handling: the book graph is NOT a pure tree; a naive recursive render of relink/fuite edges infinite-loops. Detect visited nodes and emit reference rows (↪) instead of re-expanding.
KR-031 — Shared selection: outline and canvas must read/write the SAME selection (node:selected), not two mirrors, or the panels desync (re-asserts KR-024).
KR-032 — Outline is a view over BookService; never hold a private copy of the tree that can drift (re-asserts KR-020).
KR-011 — No raw localStorage; view mode via UIPreferencesService (global config KR-111).
KR-013 — Build the row list in render/memo from book data, not a useEffect-synced state mirror (global config KR-113).
A11y — full keyboard navigation (roving tabindex), and traversal order must be stable and meaningful for screen readers.

resolved_decisions: Outline and canvas are two visualizations of the same book and share one selection source; the user explicitly asked for a canvas ↔ outline toggle.
Relink targets are reference rows, not duplicated subtrees.
open_questions: Traversal/ordering when a node has multiple parents (convergence): order under its first-authored parent, or list once at min depth? (Leaning first-authored parent.)
